cleared.check: Table row 0, the source both rows rest on. Which places in src turn a balance change that no caller paid into a credit, and which turn a transfer into a loss.
cleared.result: Only two. sync(X) stores X.balanceOf(PoolManager) in transient storage (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), and _settle credits the caller with balanceOfSelf minus that stored value in checked arithmetic, then resets the synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:357-362). For address(0), sync only resets the currency and _settle credits msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:281-283, 352-354); the native balance is never read for settlement. take debits the caller the named amount and calls transfer (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:44-86). The PoolManager has no receive or fallback function (no receive or fallback declaration in src/, searched this cycle), so native value enters it only through settle, settleFor, SELFDESTRUCT, block level credits and protocol mints. Consequences that hold on every network: (a) a balance rise between sync and settle of an ERC-20 is credited to whoever calls settle, whatever caused it; (b) a fall between sync and settle makes the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert, which only stops the caller's own settle; (c) a native rise is never credited; (d) a rise that lands before sync is inside the reserves sync records; (e) a rise that lands in another transaction cannot fall between sync and settle, because the synced slots are transient (A1, checked on every network in earlier cycles). So the only rows that matter are features that run inside a user transaction and raise the balanceOf of an ERC-20 currency the PoolManager holds, and features that make a transfer move a different amount than it reports.

cleared.check: Table row 4, Arc USDC face rounding, now with the forced send tested live (the earlier clearance said SELFDESTRUCT on Arc was untested). At block 33,459,430 the PoolManager held 2,446,663,383,620,124,987,809,451 wei, a remainder of 124,987,809,451 below the next face unit. One bracket: sync(0x3600), forced inflow of 875,012,190,549 wei, settle, native take of the same 875,012,190,549 wei (scripts/arcround.py, out/arcround.json).
cleared.result: The mechanism is live and unprofitable. The face rose by 1 unit, settle credited 1 face unit (10^12 wei), and the native delta was -875,012,190,549, so the round gained 124,987,809,451 wei, 0.000000125 USDC, taken from the native remainder that belongs to native claims. The gain per round is below 10^12 wei because the face is floor(balance / 10^12). The forced send alone needs a CREATE (32,000 gas) or a call to a funded contract that self destructs (at least about 7,600 gas), and the block base fee read at that block was 20 gwei, the floor Arc documents, so the forced send of one round costs at least 1.5 x 10^14 wei, more than 150 times the largest possible gain of 10^12 wei and more than 1,200 times the gain of this round. Arc does not serve eth_simulateV1 (method not supported), so the gas of the bracket was not measured; the bound uses the forced send only. web3_clientVersion answered arc/v1 before and after.

cleared.result: Nothing. Celo debits and credits st.msg.From, the transaction sender (celo_state_transition.go, fetched this session), before and after execution, and an earlier cycle saw debitGasFees refuse every non VM caller. Tempo collects the fee from the fee payer before execution and credits the refund to the same fee payer, and a fee payer must sign (spec-fee.md, fetched this session). Arc charges native USDC to the sender. The PoolManager has code and no key, so it is never a sender or a fee payer, and none of these debits or credits runs between a sync and a settle. The sponsor rows are untestable by eth_call, because eth_call charges no fee; they rest on the client source and the specification. F-144 records a Celo refund quirk that pays the sender only.

cleared.check: Table row 8, OP Stack deposits and the Lagoon post execution refunds.
cleared.result: Nothing. A deposit mints its value to its from account before its own execution, and the mint stays even if execution fails (deposits.html, fetched this session); a deposit is its own transaction, so it cannot fall between a sync and a settle of another one. Under Lagoon's sequencer defined metering the refund is credited to tx.from in a post execution transaction appended at the end of the block (sdm.html, fetched this session). The PoolManager is never a deposit sender or a transaction sender, F-140 records the governance path that can make it one. Lagoon is not active, so the refund row is untestable until 11 January 2027.

cleared.result: Nothing. The fee recipient or coinbase is chosen by the proposer or sequencer (operator), and the credit is applied after the transaction. cleared.check: Table rows 12 and 13, a change between a take and the settle that pays for it, and a change inside a hook callback.
cleared.result: A sync placed before a take of the same currency records the higher balance, so the settle after the take reverts on the checked subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 unless the caller repays more than it took; this stops only the caller's own transaction (and the shared transaction case of F-071). A sync placed after the take records the lower balance and the repayment is credited exactly, as row 6 shows live. A hook runs inside the same transaction as the swap or liquidity call (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-157), so it can trigger only the in transaction rows 1, 3 and 4, whose credit is the forced value the triggering party paid itself (or the Arc dust of row 4). Relays that deliver someone else's bridge payment to the PoolManager inside a caller's sync and settle are F-137 and were not retested.

leadResults.answer: The table is laid out in cleared rows 0 to 13. No row gives an ordinary account a credit it did not pay for or makes another account's settle or take fail, beyond what F-137 (relayed bridge payments) and F-071 (a leftover sync in a shared transaction) already record. Tested live this cycle through the deployed PoolManager on its real state: forced native inflow between sync(address(0)) and settle on 20 networks (credit 0), native take and settle with value on 20 (exact), the native face rows on OP Mainnet, Zora, Celo, Polygon and Arc (credit equals the caller's own forced value, settle with value reverts at src/PoolManager.sol:356), the absent face on six OP Stack networks (sync reverts), Arc's rounding with a live forced send (gain 124,987,809,451 wei per round against a forced send cost above 1.5 x 10^14 wei), and take, sync, repay and settle round trips on 24 protocol and wrapped tokens on 18 networks (exact; one Tempo token frozen as F-065 records). Resting on reading: gas fee debit and refund in tokens on Celo, Tempo and Arc (eth_call charges no fee), OP deposits, system transactions between user transactions, block rewards and withdrawals, Lagoon refunds and relays (not active), CAS20 (not active until 8 December), Tempo virtual addresses and zone portals (T15 unpublished), Avalanche multicoin.
